summary.headline: Neogen Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 42% YoY to INR 296 crore and EBITDA 51% to INR 45 crore; battery chemicals revenue reached INR 37 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 42% YoY to INR 296 crore and EBITDA rose 51% to INR 45 crore, with standalone EBITDA up 54% to INR 54 crore at an 18.6% margin. Consolidated PAT rose 144% to INR 8 crore, while standalone PAT rose 127% to INR 21 crore, with higher interest and depreciation weighing on consolidated profit. Battery chemicals (Neogen Ionics) revenue reached INR 37 crore versus INR 5 crore a year earlier, and management reiterated its FY27 battery target of INR 250-300 crore. The company completed a INR 600 crore QIP, received a CRISIL outlook upgrade to A-stable, and approved an Organolithium capacity doubling at Patancheru.

segments.name: Standalone / Neogen Chemicals (base business)
segments.commentary: Standalone EBITDA INR 54 crore at 18.6% margin; management guides 18-20% EBITDA margin for the base business. H1 FY27 base revenue indicated at over INR 550 crore.

segments.name: Battery chemicals (Neogen Ionics)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 37 crore vs INR 5 crore YoY, versus Q1 about INR 17 crore; still at fixed-cost absorption stage, with EBITDA breakeven targeted in the next financial year. Mostly salt; electrolyte under 5-10% of the battery revenue.

segments.name: Organolithium
segments.commentary: Running at about 25 tonnes per month on a 300 tonnes per annum base, described as close to or above full utilisation; revenue not disclosed.

guidance_outlook: FY27 battery chemicals revenue INR 250-300 crore (earlier target INR 300 crore), with Q3 expected above Q2 and Q4 stronger still.
FY27 consolidated revenue about INR 1,350-1,400 crore; base business FY27 about INR 1,100 crore plus, raised by INR 50-100 crore versus earlier INR 950-1,050 crore guidance.
FY28 base business revenue about INR 1,200-1,300 crore; battery revenue above INR 1,000 crore, with upside to INR 1,200-1,500 crore to be clarified by Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28.
FY28 consolidated net debt expected INR 1,300-1,500 crore, depending on lithium and other prices.
Battery business targets about 90 days working capital cycle; standalone inventory days targeted at about 180 by end-FY27, 140-160 in FY28, and 110-140 in FY29-30.
Organolithium expansion (300 to 600 tpa, capex up to INR 45 crore) expected to add INR 50-75 crore revenue next year and INR 150-200 crore once fully ramped, depending on lithium prices.
Long-term target of around INR 500 crore-plus EBITDA on INR 2,500-3,000 crore revenue at full utilisation by FY29, with 20%+ ROCE on INR 1,800-2,000 crore investment.
capex_capacity: Organolithium capacity to double from 300 to 600 tpa at Patancheru, Telangana, capex up to INR 45 crore; completion targeted by end of H1 FY28.
Dahej facility rebuilt; trial runs underway, commercial production expected shortly within FY27 and full utilisation from next quarter.
Electrolyte plant mechanically complete with trial runs begun; Pakhajan salt plant trial production targeted December 2026 and significant volumes by February/March 2027.

Neogen Ionics business transfer agreement for lithium-ion electrolyte salt (incl. LiPF6) from step-down subsidiary NML at INR 245 crore cash consideration, including INR 77 crore already infused by Morita via preference allotment.
Indian cell capacity of about 60 GWh expected online by end-FY27/early FY28, implying about 3,000 tonnes of electrolyte salt demand; installed salt capacity about 30,000 tonnes.
Next capacity decision on salt expected Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28, with a salt plant minimum size of 3,000-5,000 tonnes and 15-18 months lead time.
demand_pricing: Revenue from international salt demand: five US electrolyte makers; three have completed Dahej audits, two commercial supply commenced; fifth expected to approve Pakhajan site.
US 45X tax credit drives shift from FEOC to non-FEOC supply from 2027; management expects Neogen plus about four other non-Chinese suppliers as major salt suppliers.
Management expects the US salt demand from Q4 FY27 onward, with about 80% of the 5,500 tonne lithium salt capacity sold externally; India electrolyte customers Ola (approved) and Exide (in trials).
Lithium pricing is pass-through: quarterly reset for long-term contracts; monthly reset or fixed 3-9 month pricing with advances for new customers.
Battery requirement: India demand expected around 95-100 GWh next year per MHI report; management expects demand for FY29-30 output to already be visible in FY28.
Competition: management argues new Indian entrants face about two years to set up a plant and secure approvals; Neogen holds about 30,000 tonnes installed electrolyte salt capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline and revenue ramp for Organolithium expansion (INR 45 crore capex, INR 150-200 crore revenue)?
qa_highlights.answer: Completion targeted by end of H1 FY28; contributes INR 50-75 crore next year and full INR 150-200 crore in the year after; current run rate about 300 tonnes.

qa_highlights.question: FY28 net debt level?
qa_highlights.answer: Gopikrishnan Sarathy guided FY28 consolidated net debt of INR 1,300-1,500 crore, depending on lithium and other prices; the INR 152 crore insurance claim is expected in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Update on battery revenue guidance and international salt demand?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 battery revenue INR 250-300 crore depending on electrolyte volumes from Ola and Exide and Pakhajan; Q3 to be better than Q2 (INR 37 crore).

qa_highlights.question: Split of battery revenue between salt and electrolyte?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly salt; electrolyte is less than 5-10% of the battery revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Consolidated vs standalone revenue gap (INR 296 crore vs INR 288 crore) and inventory build?
qa_highlights.answer: Inter-unit transfers of raw materials from Neogen Chemicals to Neogen Ionics (about INR 18-20 crore); inventory rise due to Dahej rebuild and toll manufacturing. Inventory days target about 180 by end-FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Use of QIP proceeds and further expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Primarily for deleveraging (term loans, INR 200 crore bond repayment); next salt capacity decision in FY28 depending on US and India demand.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Base business margin guided at 18-20%; Neogen Ionics expected EBITDA positive soon, PBT positive in the next financial year.

risks_watch: Battery ramp-up depends on 60 GWh of Indian cell capacity coming online by Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28; management acknowledged uncertainty on stabilisation timing (six months to two years).
Battery FY27 guidance is at the lower end of the range if Indian electrolyte customers (Exide in trials) slip; the company may rely on Pakhajan salt volumes, whose approval timing is uncertain.
Inventory days elevated during Dahej rebuild and toll manufacturing; working capital needs rise with battery ramp.
Net debt rises to INR 1,300-1,500 crore in FY28 from INR 1,095 crore, with capex needs for Pakhajan, Dahej and a possible FY28-29 salt expansion.
Lithium price pass-through and US FEOC policy changes; Chinese capacity build in the US could change competitive dynamics.
Consolidated PAT impacted by higher interest and depreciation; management did not share a detailed cash flow bridge.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and long-term opportunity, with specific but conditional guidance; the management was more cautious on near-term battery volumes and FY28 cash flows, which it said would be shared by email rather than on the call.
key_quotes: Our standalone profitability is even better as consolidated performance reflects initial fixed cost absorption at Neogen Ionic where the revenues scale up and capacity utilisation continue to ramp up.
So together, we do not see a challenge in crossing INR 1,000 crore plus revenue.
It will be very difficult to describe all this over a call right now.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Base business EBITDA margin guided at 18-20% and standalone margin was 18.6% in Q2; Neogen Ionics expected EBITDA positive soon, with breakeven targeted next financial year, though battery is still at fixed-cost absorption stage.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Dahej rebuild in trial runs with commercial production expected within FY27, Pakhajan salt trial production Dec 2026 with significant volumes Feb/Mar 2027, and Organolithium doubling from 300 to 600 tpa (capex up to INR 45 crore) due by end H1 FY28.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Battery revenue rose to INR 37 crore in Q2 from INR 17 crore in Q1 and management expects Q3 above Q2 and Q4 stronger still, toward FY27 battery target of INR 250-300 crore; Organolithium already near full utilisation at 25 tpm.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Next salt capacity decision expected Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28 (minimum 3,000-5,000 tonnes, 15-18 months lead time) against installed salt capacity of about 30,000 tonnes and 60 GWh Indian cell demand implying about 3,000 tonnes of salt.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Standalone FY27 revenue guidance already raised by INR 50-100 crore to INR 1,100 crore plus, and standalone H1 base revenue indicated above INR 550 crore; battery target was cut to INR 250-300 crore, which limits upside on the consolidated line.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Battery FY27 target is already at the lower end if Exide trials slip or Pakhajan approval is delayed, and management admitted six months to two years of uncertainty on Indian cell stabilisation.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Electrolyte plant mechanically complete with trial runs begun and Exide in trials, but electrolyte is under 5-10% of battery revenue, so launch impact is small in the window.

rows.label: US salt supply contracts (FEOC shift)
rows.why: Five US electrolyte makers in the pipeline, two commercial supply already started, three audits done, and management expects US salt demand from Q4 FY27 with about 80% of 5,500 tonne lithium salt capacity sold externally.

rows.label: Net debt rises to INR 1,300-1,500 crore in FY28
rows.why: Consolidated net debt is INR 1,095 crore at Sep 2026 and guided up to INR 1,300-1,500 crore in FY28 for Pakhajan, Dahej and possible salt expansion, with INR 152 crore insurance claim expected in Q3.

rows.label: Neogen Ionics salt business transfer INR 245 crore
rows.why: Business transfer agreement for LiPF6 and electrolyte salt from NML at INR 245 crore cash, with INR 77 crore already infused by Morita via preference allotment.

tone.note: Management was confident on base-business guidance (raised to INR 1,100 crore plus, margins 18-20%) and long-term demand, but cautious on near-term battery volumes and FY28 cash flow, which it deferred to email; analysts pressed on the battery ramp and inventory and working-capital build.
